I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.

highlights.title: Barcelona move clear at the top after Fermín López’s double stuns Atlético Madrid
highlights.summary: They had been in a battle, they had been behind and they had been on edge, but Barcelona found a way through, holding on to their place at the top of the table and holding the doubts at bay for another day.
body: At a noisy, intense Metropolitano, against an even more intense Atlético, they went behind to a Giuliano Simeone goal and for a while in a frantic first half it looked like there may be no way back. But they found it, two goals from Fermín López either side of half-time leading them to the kind of victory that brings a reward beyond just the points. It had been a long night, but they had made it.

Atlético flew into this, fuelled by the noise. They did more inside three minutes than in 90 against Bayern Munich in midweek. A superb clearance from Pau Cubarsí kept them at bay in the first minute. Álex Baena curled wide in the second. And they forced a corner in the third. Barcelona were overwhelmed and exposed, unable to settle, and Diego Simeone’s side could sense it.

highlights.title: Apple is racing to make Siri more agentic
highlights.summary: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman says CEO John Ternus is pressuring AI czar Craig Federighi to accelerate the Siri roadmap and deliver a powerful AI agent that can compete with OpenAI's Dots or Meta's Muse.
body: Future versions of Siri will be able to control third-party apps and perform more complex tasks.

Two significant improvements are expected to be made to Siri in the coming months. One will give the assistant fine-grained control over Apple’s first-party apps, allowing it to do things like rotate and crop images in Photos and organize Safari tabs. Those capabilities are expected to land with iOS 27.3. The bigger change, integration with third-party apps, is likely to land later, in the Spring, according to Gurman. That would let Siri place an order through Grubhub or book a dinner reservation through OpenTable, for example.

Dots, Muse and Grok can keep track of goals, determine what needs to happen next and continue pursuing objectives without the user initiating every individual step. Apple ultimately wants to go in this direction, I’m told, and I believe the company could make Siri more like an agent as early as next year — not that it has much of a choice, given current consumer and market demands.

body: Best Casting Predictions Commentary (Updated: Nov. 8, 2026): Casting is only in its second year as an Oscar category and if voters just default to whichever best picture front-runner had the splashiest ensemble, the whole point of the award might be flawed. One of the two films that stand out in this category sense, are “ Being Heumann,” Siân Heder’s Apple drama about Judy Heumann and the 1977 San Francisco sit-in that forced the government to enforce disability rights and “La Bola Negra,” Los Javis’ Netflix epic that threads three gay men across three eras of Spain.

For Heder’s film, casting directors Bernie Telsey and Adam Caldwell put more than 20 disabled actors on screen around breakout Ruth Madeley’s Judy, a lot of them with little or no acting experience, which is a bigger swing than any other star-studded ensemble.

Over in Spain, Eva Leira and Yolanda Serrano delivered Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi a cast where the pop singer Guitarricadelafuente makes his acting debut alongside newcomers Milo Quifes and Carlos González, then surrounded them with legends like Penélope Cruz and a Spanish-speaking Glenn Close. That’s discovery.

highlights.title: Why Austin Butler Cannot Drive the Iconic Black Ferrari in Miami Vice '85
highlights.summary: New videos from the set of Miami Vice ‘85 reveal Austin Butler’s Sonny Crockett and Michael B. Jordan's Ricardo Tubbs driving a white Ferrari Testarossa, the wrong car for the period of the TV series that director Joseph Kosinski’s film is retelling. And there’s likely a legal reason for that.
body: In the show’s canon, Crockett’s cars were seized assets from criminals and loaned to him by the Miami-Dade Police Department as part of his undercover identity. The department supplied Crockett with a white 1986 Ferrari Testarossa in the second episode of Season 3.

The Daytona Spyder seen on the show, however, was a replica built on a Corvette C3 chassis since Ferrari North America refused to provide the show with an authentic model. Ferrari launched a legal battle against the show and the replica builder, McBurnie Coachcraft, citing trademark infringement and brand dilution.

“They eventually settled the dispute, winning broad legal protections for their trademarks and even the ‘shape and profile’ of the car,” recapped by @CinemaIsLife on X. “As a part of the settlement they donated two authentic Testarossas (their new flagship car) to the production—but only on the condition that the fake Daytona be dramatically blown up on national television.”
It would appear then that Universal is simply avoiding another legal headache by jettisoning the Daytona Spyder from Miami Vice ‘85 and going with the white Testarossa even though it violates canon.

highlights.title: Caffeine off the clock: six ways baristas make coffee at home (and one they all hate)
highlights.summary: What do people who spend all day making coffee use when off the clock? Their solutions are simpler than you’d expect. The best instant coffees – from from powders to pastes. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: Karl Stuebe, barista and co-owner of Home Coffee Roasters in San Francisco, never really clocks out. Every morning at his little home coffee station, he brews a cup and judges it. If it comes out “a little bit bright” (a coffee pro term for “overly acidic”), Stuebe writes a note and tries something different the next day. “I’m always measuring what the quality is like,” he says. “I like to keep testing my palate every day.”

For many baristas and cafe owners like Stuebe, coffee isn’t a drink; it’s a calling. But what do they use to brew at home, away from their $26,000 La Marzocco espresso machines? I asked baristas in the west coast coffee meccas of San Francisco and Portland, Oregon. Here are their favorites, including some surprisingly inexpensive options – and one method they all despise.

Cobi Williams is one of Stuebe’s baristas at Home Coffee Roasters in San Francisco’s Chinatown. Williams chooses his morning brewing method by “how lazy I’m feeling”, he says. On his sleepiest days it’s a French press. “I just wait while it sits.” All you need are coarse grounds and hot water; no paper filters needed, not even electricity. Steep for four minutes, then press.

body: "I have a paranoid answer for this," Eisenberg said when asked if he's nervous about the technology. "I’m totally paranoid. I sometimes experiment with AI to see whether it's good at writing. And it's still not.

"I’m paranoid, so I check and it still isn't. Thank God. I say, 'Write a scene like this.' I'm just testing it to make sure it's bad, and it's still bad. So I'm relieved, but, like, how far away is it from being good? How far are we from a kid putting on a pair of goggles and saying, 'I want to watch a movie about me where I rob a bank and then kiss the girl I’m in love with at school. Here are pictures of her, here are pictures of me' and then they press play? I'm paranoid about that."

highlights.title: Soul Glo’s Diaspora Problems is a hardcore record like no other
highlights.summary: Soul Glo has a new record called NA I'M GON GRAB ALLAT coming out in January, and I, for one, can not wait. While two singles have dropped, it's not enough to truly tide me over, so I've been revisiting Songs to Yeet at the Sun and my favorite album of 2022 - Diaspora Problems.
body: The record barely lets up from here on out. “Coming Correct” opens with a cough and a steady 808, giving you literally three seconds to catch your breath before Jordan jumps on the mic shouting, “I try to listen the way, I wanna be listened to.” The song starts stacking elements quickly, reaching full firestorm by 25 seconds in, and then does let up for the rest of its three-minute runtime.

The front chunk of the record is just perfect unrelenting hardcore song after perfect unrelenting hardcore song. Jordan’s crazed charisma is undeniable as he ricochets between leftist rhetoric, goofy bits about smoking weed, and vulnerable explorations of his struggles with depression. You’d be forgiven for struggling to keep up with his rapid-fire delivery, which owes almost as much to modern rappers as it does to classic hardcore acts like Minor Threat or Bad Brains.

Track six, “Driponomics,” fully embraces those more modern influences with trap snares, wall-rattling 808 kicks, and a guest verse from Mother Maryrose. The sampled guitar calls to mind the sax squeals favored by the Bomb Squad… just heavier.
points: Soul Glo has a new record called NA I'M GON GRAB ALLAT coming out in January, and I, for one, can not wait.

highlights.title: World Models Will Soon Be Inescapable. Here’s What You Need to Know
highlights.summary: Moving AI from text to 3D space, world models simulate real-world physics to teach robots and autonomous cars how to navigate reality.
body: It’s 2016, and you’re wandering around the neighborhood at dusk. On the prowl, you’re swiping on a smartphone to catch that elusive Snorlax and grow your collection in Pokémon Go. You, alongside hundreds of millions of other players, are enjoying a mixed-reality game built around lovable characters. What you don’t realize is that these scans of your environment will one day help robots navigate obstacles and interact with objects.

Niantic, the creator of Pokémon Go, sold the game last year and pivoted hard into one of Silicon Valley’s buzziest AI topics right now: world models. “We’re very much about reconstructing the real world,” says Brian McClendon, Niantic Spatial’s chief technology officer. He hopes to leverage its trove of world data to build replicas. Unlike the text-based nature of large language models, world models use visual inputs and can generate digital environments that simulate physics.

Sage has guided Palace to only two wins from their 10 Premier League games this season and they have the league’s worst defensive record, with 24 goals conceded so far. Although there were promising moments during the 3-1 defeat by Liverpool at Selhurst Park on Sunday, their habit of conceding goals from set pieces has not been rectified and it is understood the patience of the club’s hierarchy has worn thin despite Sage only being at the helm for 16 matches.

He is expected to become the first Premier League manager to be sacked this season on Monday. Palace are already believed to have started the process of bringing in his replacement. Frank, who was dismissed by Tottenham in February, spoke to Palace in the summer and is said to be keen for a new challenge after a successful spell at Brentford.

highlights.title: 25 Years Later, ‘Buffy the Vampire Slayer’s Best Quote Is Still the Most Inspiring Line in TV History
highlights.summary: Buffy’s story has always revolved around death. Throughout its seven-season run, Buffy Summers (Sarah Michelle Gellar) has wanted to escape from it or, boldly, return to it.
body: In the Buffy the Vampire Slayer season 5 finale, Sunnydale is collapsing, and Buffy’s allies have nowhere to go. Her little sister, Dawn (Michelle Trachtenberg), is the reason why a dangerous portal has opened, and she tries to jump in to close it. But Buffy stops her. “The hardest thing in this world is to live in it,” she tells her. “Be brave. Live. For me.”
The two share the same blood, so Buffy is capable of closing the portal on her own. She jumps in and dies. It’s a moment that closes out an arc that had been teased since season 1.

Season 5 is one of Buffy’s most emotional seasons. It’s also one of its boldest, committing to a new central dynamic: Buffy and Dawn. Maligned series creator Joss Whedon shared that he introduced Dawn as a way of giving Buffy an intense dynamic that wasn’t based in romance. After seasons of Angel, Riley, and hints of Spike, it feels like a breath of fresh air to see Buffy get mad, angry, happy, and distraught over a different type of relationship.

highlights.title: From the Archives: When Iowa Governor-Elect Rob Sand Was Shot by Steven Meisel for Vogue Italia
highlights.summary: Before winning Iowa’s gubernatorial race, Rob Sand was posing with supermodels, wearing Helmut Lang, and walking the Prada runway. Revisit his February 2004 Vogue Italia spread.
body: “Be My Baby,” by Steven Meisel, was originally published in the February 2004 issue of Vogue Italia.

With a fluffed-up quiff and a supermodel on his arm, here’s a look at Iowa’s next governor. Long before Democrat Rob Sand made political history, he was having a very different kind of moment in the spotlight, posing for Steven Meisel in the pages of Vogue Italia.

The year was 2004, and Sand was among the fresh faces who appeared in “Be My Baby,” an editorial in the February issue, photographed by Meisel and styled by Brana Wolf. Alongside Sand was a cast of rising fashion stars, including a young Caroline Trentini, with whom he posed in a series of moody, black-and-white portraits.

The concept centered on a romanticized vision of 1950s youth culture, abounding with the aforementioned rockabilly hair and lots of leather The original Italian introduction described the mood as a collision of bon ton —good manners and traditional propriety—and transgression.

highlights.summary: Former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden said he thinks innovation at Sony shouldn't come "from making a PS6 for $1,200" but from making "another PS5 for $300." As tech costs skyrocket and rumors of pricey gaming consoles swirl, the former president and CEO of Sony Interactive Entertainment America…
body: As Layden put it, "I think we have enough power in the machine."

"The innovation needs to come not from making PS6 for $1,200. It's to make another PS5 for $300," he added. "Now, that would be true innovation. This is the first platform that I've seen that has gone up in price over time. I mean, PS2, at the end of the PS2 era, it was $99. You could buy a PS2 for $99."

The PS5 launched almost exactly six years ago with two primary options for players to choose from: a base version with a disc drive for $499, and a Digital Edition for $399. What seemed like relatively fair price points in 2020 now seems almost like a steal thanks to a series of price increases in recent years. Today, buying a base PS5 directly from PlayStation costs $649, a Digital Edition costs $599, and a Pro costs an unbelievable $899 (up $200 from its reveal price ). Things get even worse when you look at retailers like GameStop.

highlights.title: Older women are as varied and individual as we have ever been | Letters
highlights.summary: Thank you, Jo Brand, for not offering us a formula for growing older, writes Dr Denise Taylor. Plus a letter from Louise Mothersole. I found Jo Brand’s reflections on approaching 70 wonderfully refreshing ( ‘It’s far too late for me to go to the gym every 10 minutes’: Jo Brand on ageing, raging…
body: We hear so much about ageing well, ageing positively and ageing successfully. We are encouraged to exercise more, eat better, remain productive, find our purpose and keep reinventing ourselves. Much of this advice is well intentioned, but collectively it can make growing older seem like another job we are expected to perform.

As a 69-year-old psychologist who researches and writes about later life, I question this narrative. Of course, looking after our health matters. But ageing isn’t a competition, and we shouldn’t have to demonstrate that we’re making the most of every remaining year.

I was particularly struck by Brand’s comments about older women being treated as though they are all alike. We are as varied, contradictory and individual as we have ever been. Some of us want adventure; others want a quieter life. Some are still working, others are delighted to have left employment behind. And our feelings about ageing can change from one day to the next.

Perhaps what makes Brand’s interview so appealing is that she doesn’t offer us a formula for growing older. She simply describes her experience, with humour, honesty and a willingness to acknowledge what is difficult.
points: Thank you, Jo Brand, for not offering us a formula for growing older, writes Dr Denise Taylor.

highlights.title: Hamilton says he overrode Ferrari pit call due to 'lack of information'
highlights.summary: Lewis Hamilton says a lack of information led to him overriding Ferrari's call for him to come into the pits as rain fell during the closing stages of the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.
body: Hamilton was running in eighth at Interlagos when heavy rain began to fall with 10 laps to go. While the leaders had already passed the pit entry by the time the rain intensified, Mercedes brought in George Russell from fifth.

Ferrari instructed Hamilton to come in, but he decided to do the opposite to the car just in front of him at the time, Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson. Hamilton's team-mate Charles Leclerc, running just behind him, came into the pits.
The seven-time world champion spun on the next lap in the treacherous conditions, before pitting at the end of it to follow his rivals onto intermediates.

While there was little at stake, as Hamilton ultimately finished ninth rather than claiming what could have been seventh if he had got past Lawson, it was the latest example of imperfect execution from the British driver and his Italia team.

highlights.title: Ocarina of Time remake datamine suggests Master Quest is on the way
highlights.summary: Ocarina of Time 's notoriously tricky Master Quest mode could be making a comeback in the new remake.
body: Dataminer MrCheeze shared a list of strings from the remake's files on Bluesky, several of which tie the tag "MQ" to dungeons like Dodongo's Cavern.
In a follow-up, as spotted by TheGamer, they pointed to further entries, including "HasMQ", "IsMQModeExist", "NewGameMQ", and "ReleaseMQ".

Fellow dataminer OatmealDome added on Twitter/X that the mode will be unlocked by owning DLC, rather than arriving in an update, though "the data is incomplete". "I can confirm that the world is mirrored and dungeons are modified (e.g. cows in Jabu-Jabu's Belly)," they said.

If you've not played it, Master Quest is a remixed version of Ocarina of Time with rearranged dungeons and tougher puzzles. It first appeared as a bonus disc on GameCube, then came back in 2011's Ocarina of Time 3D, which unlocked it after you finished the main game. That version also mirrored the whole world, which matches what OatmealDome has found, and had enemies deal double damage.

highlights.title: ‘Avedon’ Review: Ron Howard’s Thrilling Documentary About Richard Avedon, the Great Photographer Who Turned Head-On Portraits Into an Art Form
highlights.summary: "Avedon," Ron Howard’s documentary about the legendary photographer, is a fantastic movie. It’s the best documentary Ron Howard has made (my favorite before this: "The Beatles: Eight Days a Week — The Touring Years"), and it’s been edited in a way that’s so supple and artful that its technique…
body: Avedon was a paragon of high fashion and also the ultimate democratic humanist. The film explains that paradox and makes his images sing.

“Avedon” opens with an old clip of Richard Avedon, fixing that piercing bird-eye look of his into the camera as he explains, “I can say very little about photography. I follow no rules, no laws, and no advice.” He’s totally serious about that. We then get a montage, set to the funky martial beat of Spoon’s “I Turn My Camera On,” of Avedon portraits of the famous. John Lennon. Orson Welles. Michael Jordan. Elizabeth Taylor. Groucho Marx. Twiggy (in mid-air). Anjelica Huston. Marilyn Monroe lovingly embracing Arthur Miller. Truman Capote. J. Robert Oppenheimer.

highlights.title: Is this the most rubbish Christmas present ever? | Polly Hudson
highlights.summary: I thought I knew all about disappointment, having received one of the very worst presents as a child. Then I heard about ‘data gifting’ One Christmas when I was a child, my parents wrapped the presents in shiny paper.
body: The jubilation I felt at pulling off such a stealth move – being basically a master criminal in the manner of those movie jewel thieves who dodge laser tripwires – was almost immediately negated by the sinking realisation I’d ruined my own Christmas. I’d been too impatient to bear the wait, but now, with weeks still to go, all anticipation and excitement had been extinguished. Not least because my main present was – how to put this delicately? – crap.

I always struggled to get up for school, so Santa had stitched me up with an alarm clock. A fun, razzy alarm clock, but an alarm clock all the same. To clarify: no kid wants an alarm clock. It was the very definition of bleak times.

Until this week, I believed this was the most depressing Christmas present in the history of the nativity. But then I heard an advert for a mobile phone provider, which offered the suggestion of “data gifting”. This is where, brimming with festive spirit, you transfer your unused or spare data to somebody else’s device or plan, ho ho ho. A virtual, imaginary present so entirely practical the recipient probably won’t even realise when they use it.
